minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved several wetland filings and a beaver-flow device, and sent a Sunset Lane wetland review to third-party review.
minutes.summary: The commission continued three hearings to May 15, then heard a Hickory Hills beach sand RDA, a tree-removal RDA at 189 Hemlock Drive, a third-party wetland review dispute at 255 Sunny Hill Road, and an amendment at 386 Sunset Lane. It also handled certificates of compliance, enforcement updates (Fire Road 12, 205 Sunset Lane, 950 Chase Road), and several small spending approvals before adjourning near 9:48 pm.

public_comment.topic: Asked how the enforcement process works for a neighbor's dock at 607/609/611 and said the neighbor installed fences within the 30-foot no-touch zone.
Responded to the 950 Chase Road concerns, saying the shed and clearing pre-dated their 2018 purchase, the shed is on Town property, and they stopped snowmobile use.

what_happened.line: The commission approved a beaver-flow device at the Cranberry area and sent the 255 Sunny Hill Road wetland review to third-party review, then continued that hearing to May 15.
It accepted a quote for third-party wetland delineation review only at 255 Sunny Hill Road, a narrower scope than the full-scope quote the applicant had objected to.
It approved wetland filings: a beach sand RDA at Hickory Hills, a tree-removal RDA at 189 Hemlock Drive, and an order of conditions amendment at 386 Sunset Lane.
A motion to issue a notice of non-compliance at 205 Sunset Lane was not audible in the record, and staff were assigned to research the order's timing first.
The commission moved title search spending from the Kelly Fund to the timber rights fund, and approved several small purchases and a building repainting.

why_it_matters: The Kelly Fund is being kept for major land acquisitions, so routine title-search costs now come from the timber rights fund instead.
Third-party wetland review at 255 Sunny Hill Road adds a consultant step before the commission rules, and the applicant pays a deposit for it.
The commission is considering an earlier meeting end time because the administrator cannot support meetings past 10 pm, which could affect how long hearings can run.
watch_next: Continued hearings at 390 Howard Street, 171 Arbor Street, 141 Hemlock Drive and 255 Sunny Hill Road return on May 15.
The 205 Sunset Lane non-compliance question and the 950 Chase Road drone photos are due for review at the next meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nearly every vote and on both money figures that were voted ($1,000 title-search transfer, $6,400 repaint), and most differences are caption mishearings of names, addresses and digits. The one substantive difference is the 189 Hemlock Drive vote: the official minutes record a roll call with Mike voting no and Rich B. recused, while ours records a plain pass with no dissent or recusal.
